source.title: Active Inference, homeostatic regulation and adaptive behavioural control

confidence_rationale: The closest formal articulation of REE's drive layer: homeostatic set-points enter as priors that 'act as drives or goals to enslave action', and multiple control processes (Pavlovian, habitual, goal-directed) are cast as hierarchical contextualisations rather than competitors with a hard boundary. This grounds MECH-394's soft-competitive (not winner-take-all) framing and the homeostatic-vs-exploratory balance the claim cites loosely as 'Pezzulo 2014'. Held at 0.68 because it is a theoretical review proposing a framework, not an empirical result or a worked arbitration policy; it licenses the architecture, it does not test it.
failure_signatures: The framework dissolves the mechanistic distinction between control processes rather than specifying an explicit arbitration rule; it tells you drives-as-priors compete softly via precision-weighting but does not pin down the WTA-vs-blend decision MECH-394 must make, so it under-determines the policy.

As a normative active-inference account it predicts behaviour minimises expected free energy; if REE's substrate cannot represent the homeostatic set-points as priors with calibrated precision, the soft-competition the framework promises will not emerge and arbitration could collapse to whichever drive has the largest raw error.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Within Active Inference, homeostatic and allostatic regulation is achieved by treating interoceptive set-points as priors that drive action to fulfil them; Pavlovian, habitual, and goal-directed processes are successive hierarchical contextualisations of the same sensorimotor inference rather than mechanistically distinct controllers, and priors act as drives/goals that enslave action via precision-weighting.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-394 asserts arbitration is soft-competitive over context/satiation/competition/developmental-phase, not a fixed single-axis winner. Pezzulo, Rigoli & Friston supply the formal scaffold: if each drive axis is a homeostatic prior, then multiple simultaneously-active drives are multiple priors competing for control via their precisions, and precision-weighting is the soft-competition mechanism -- the same vocabulary REE uses (precision-selection, soft-competitive disinhibition). The hierarchical-contextualisation move grounds MECH-394's 'over context' orchestration variable: context sets which drive-prior is most precise. The exploratory-vs-homeostatic balance the claim attributes to 'Pezzulo 2014' is articulated here as the trade-off between epistemic (information-seeking) and pragmatic (homeostatic) value, cross-referencing ARC-073's play-to-real competence-saturation criterion.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a theoretical review, not an empirical study or a simulation of multidrive arbitration; it licenses the architecture (drives-as-priors, soft precision-weighted competition) without specifying or testing the explicit arbitration rule MECH-394 needs. The claim's '2014' citation resolves to this 2015 Prog Neurobiol review (and the broader Pezzulo homeostatic active-inference program); the year drift is noted. Treating the framework as evidence FOR a particular policy (e.g. precision-weighted blend over WTA) would over-read it.
mapping.source_context: Conceptual synthesis / review uniting Active Inference (Bayesian perception-action) with associative-learning accounts of homeostatic and behavioural control.

confidence_components.notes: Influential Prog Neurobiol review. Mapping_fidelity high on vocabulary alignment (priors-as-drives, precision-weighted soft competition) but it is a framework not a result; source_quality reflects review status, not primary data.
